string-array.name: municipalities_array
string-array.item: Beijing is the capital city of China. As the national political and cultural centre, it hosts many world‑famous historical landmarks including the Forbidden City. It has a long history spanning hundreds of dynasties and combines traditional heritage with modern urban development.

Shanghai is China’s largest metropolis and major international financial hub located on the east coast. It mixes classic colonial‑era buildings with towering modern skyscrapers. It plays a vital role in national trade, finance and international cultural exchanges.

Chongqing is a large inland direct‑administered municipality in southwest China. Known for mountainous terrain, hot‑pot culture and large river transport systems. It has experienced rapid modernisation while preserving unique local folk customs.

Tianjin is a northern coastal municipality close to Beijing. It features a mix of western‑style historical architecture and modern port facilities. As an important industrial and logistics centre, it supports the economic development of northern China.
